description: Quanthelix is a solo, student-led team focused on AI, statistical analysis, and data-driven scientific discovery. As a high school student with experience in quantitative research, Python, and interactive data visualization, I have developed independent research projects and analytical tools, including MarketLens. Through NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I aim to apply rigorous statistical methods and innovative technology to explore Earth system trends and uncover meaningful patterns.
summary: Earth Clues is an interactive web app that turns NASA Earth science data into accessible, country-level climate insights. Users can explore 17 environmental variables across 47 Asian countries, inspect Kazakhstan’s 2016–2025 trends, compare each variable with the closest country-level series, and view cautious projections with uncertainty ranges. The app connects notable patterns to role-specific questions and possible next steps for farmers, water managers, planners, and residents. Its results are screening clues—not causal findings, safety thresholds, or definitive forecasts.
details:
Earth Clues is an interactive web application that turns NASA Earth observations into understandable local climate clues. Built for the “Be an Earth System Trend Detective” challenge, it starts with a Kazakhstan case study and allows users to explore 17 environmental variables across 47 Asian countries.

The project investigates four questions: What changed? Which countries show similar patterns? What might happen if the observed patterns continued? What should people investigate or consider doing next?

How it works

Earth Clues uses country-area data from NASA MERRA-2 and NASA GLDAS Noah. It organizes variables into four groups: atmosphere and precipitation, soil moisture, snow and water movement, and energy exchange. Users select a country and variable through an interactive map and explore annual records, seasonal patterns, comparisons, and explanations.

The analysis uses ten complete years, 2016–2025. It distinguishes annual averages from annual accumulated quantities and excludes incomplete years from annual comparisons. Each country’s recent values are compared with its own reference period to identify departures from its typical range.

For Kazakhstan, the application examines temperature, precipitation, and root-zone soil moisture together. It separates changes between the first and last years from trends fitted to the entire record. Cross-country comparisons are calculated separately for each variable, helping users investigate similarities without assuming that two countries share the same overall climate.

The application also provides conditional linear estimates with 95% prediction intervals. These illustrate what continuation of a fitted pattern would imply; they are not definitive forecasts.

Benefits and intended impact

Earth Clues connects data exploration with questions relevant to farmers, residents, planners, and water managers. Explanations describe what variables mean, while role-based suggestions identify possible priorities such as protecting soil moisture, monitoring seasonal water availability, and reviewing water infrastructure.

Environmental reports provide additional context for interpreting local conditions. This context is presented separately from the statistical results: a national time series alone cannot establish the cause of an environmental change.

Our intended impact is to make Earth-system evidence easier to understand and discuss, particularly in Kazakhstan and Central Asia. The application is designed for people without specialist scientific training, while retaining units, data sources, methods, and uncertainty information.

Tools and development

We developed Earth Clues using Python and Streamlit, with Altair for interactive charts. GitHub hosts the project code, and Streamlit Community Cloud hosts the public application. The project uses existing Earth-observation datasets and requires no custom hardware.

Creativity and design considerations

Earth Clues connects global data with a local investigation. Instead of treating temperature, water, soil, and energy as isolated topics, it lets users explore their signals within one application and move from observations toward informed questions.

We considered accessibility, multilingual explanations, appropriate units, incomplete records, country-level aggregation, and the limitations of a short reference period. Similarity does not establish causation, and national averages can hide local differences. Action suggestions therefore serve as starting points for local assessment.

The project is under continuing development, with the longer-term goal of extending coverage beyond Asia.

Earth Clues is an independent project by Quanthelix team, Zhanbota Erlan, using NASA data. It is not an official NASA product.
